title: Adi Shankara
summary: Shankara was an Indian philosopher regarded as the most authoritative thinker of Advaita Vedanta, which reads the Upanishads as teaching a nondual brahman identical with the self. His dates are debated: 788–820 CE in older scholarship, c. 700–750 in later work. Hagiographies written centuries later place his birth at Kalady in Kerala and say he died aged thirty-two.

uncertainty.note: Range spans the two competing datings: c. 700–750 CE (Nakamura) and 788–820 CE (older scholarship). Birth and death years are not independently recorded.

as_recorded.value: Early scholars placed him from 788–820 CE.
argues for an earlier date of 700–750 CE

where.historical_name: Kalāḍi, Kerala (birthplace as given in later hagiographies)

importance.justification: Described as the most authoritative philosopher of Advaita Vedanta, with commentaries on the Brahmasutras, the Bhagavadgita and principal Upanishads.

reviewer_note: Least sure: dates (788–820 vs c. 700–750) and birthplace. SEP attributes Kalady only to hagiographies composed centuries after his death, so the pin is traditional with a 50 km radius. The four-math tradition is omitted because encyclopedia.com and SEP differ on it.
